title: Closure of pair-ferromagnet chains inside the Lee-Yang class
note: The closure of pair-ferromagnet laws is a proper subclass of the Lee-Yang class (n >= 5: FK cone; limit sense: GHS), but the separating conditions (GHS, FK cone) are kernel-side positivity that Phi and the DH kernel both satisfy, so they carry no zero information. Whether membership of Phi in the closure is strictly stronger than RH is not established. R1 holds at stage level only.
lesson: Ferromagnet membership is strictly stronger than Lee-Yang, but the conditions that separate them (GHS, FK cone) are kernel-side positivity that Phi and DH both satisfy, so they give no handle on zeros. R1 holds at stage level only (product over prime sites; DH stage 55 of 55 off the line; Beurling energies also pass). R3 fails: U, sign twists and Beurling pass every stage, and E_a and T-NR pass at small log M through heat contraction.

lesson: The Lee-Yang stage's index 0 is the inequality Re D_M'/D_M > -(log M)/2, which becomes empty as M grows; the conductor factor that makes stages self-dual erases the limit (symbol -> -1). Any limit step from zero-free product stages is Hurwitz plus local boundedness of pole-renormalised stages, which is RH restated as the PNT error term. r1 holds only at stage level (zero-free stages need the Euler product); the U control fails at the open step, not at a proved one. title: Joint multi-delay (Bohr torus) inner sections of the prime chain
note: Within the unipotent chain family a block of prime sections has rank-one additive J-defect, so joint contractivity is the scalar inequality Re U_P <= Re G and twists are torus translations. For finite P no positive-real function of several prime delays can be split off xi'/xi (Theorem B). The sharp section fails at fixed sigma < 1 for large Q (pole term). The Fejer-tapered section is an explicit-formula identity equivalent to RH that uses no multiplicativity. Open: infinite P, general J-inner linear-fractional sections, DH analogue.
lesson: Sections of the prime chain commute and have rank-one additive defect, so grouping primes adds no freedom: joint contractivity is the largest-value inequality itself. What separates zeta's phases from twists is one-sidedness of the prime sum coming from the zero measure via the functional equation (visible with Fejer weights), not Kronecker structure of finitely many primes; that is a restatement of RH. Multiplicativity entered only in a no-go (point evaluation of H at p^-1/2).

title: Positive-definiteness of log zeta(sigma+iu) left of Re s = 1
note: The compensated positivity CP(sigma) is equivalent to 'no zeros with Re s > sigma'; the direction CP => zero-free uses only the prime-free half-line x < 0. Raw positive-definiteness fails for every sigma < 1. The PD kernel ends at the pole on the diagonal, so there is no transport in sigma (three named mechanisms fail; no general no-transport theorem).
lesson: Left of the pole, positivity of the compensated transform splits into a support (causality) condition on the prime-free half-line, which is the zero-free statement itself, and a sign condition on the atoms, which is automatic. Sign-positive twists, Beurling and E_a (sigma > 1/2+a, measured) pass, so the property separates zeta from them only through their zeros. Fixed-order minors hold under zero-freeness but do not exclude a single zero (reasoning only).

note: [V_n, G_tau] = G_tau(exp(tau l(u+l)/4) - 1)V_n; the eigen-defect order in tau is 1 iff coefficients are completely multiplicative at p, else 0, and no higher order exists. lesson: The Hecke eigen-property is carried along by the shear (conjugated operators keep it at every tau); the only thing special at tau = 0 is that Hecke operators are translations, which is "completely multiplicative ordinary Dirichlet series" restated. Defect order in tau is 0 or 1 and cannot separate zeta from any completely multiplicative control. tau = 0 is the boundary of the sheared prime expansion's convergence domain, approached from the side where the conclusion is false, with l^1 size about exp(1/(4|tau|)).

note: For a finite set S of primes, jointly S-primitive tests are dense (L^2 and Q) in the test class, so the infimum of Q/norm^2 over primitive tests equals the infimum over all tests: the restriction neither helps nor costs. The Gram matrix of dilations does not contain the function's coefficients. All-prime Hecke sums lie in the radical of the zero sum. lesson: Hecke/Moebius operators are translation multipliers with no zeros in the open strip, so restricting a translation-invariant form (Weil/Q_L) to primitive tests is a congruence and changes nothing; the orthogonalisation step is function-independent. Any multiplicative mechanism must act where the cutoff fails to commute with Hecke (window defect), and that formula is also kernel-independent. Reusable tool: plib.py computes Q_L from primes alone in an orthonormal basis (Loewner form) for zeta and four controls, validated against zero sums to 1e-12.

title: Windowed semidefinite coupling of Pick positivity with the explicit formula
note: The real-node Pick matrix is linear in the zero measure, on-line pairs add PSD terms, and the LMI never contains the primes; so the joint window SDP equals the explicit-formula LP (delta*_joint = delta*_EF, T in 1e2..1e6, K <= 24; grid-certified on five node families, node-uniform statement open at (100,24)). No exclusion for L <= L*/2 at any height. Untested: an LMI whose on-line terms are not sign-definite (sector matrices P+-B).
lesson: A positivity LMI that is linear in the zero measure and monotone in on-line mass cannot couple to the explicit formula: it acts only where it already excludes the configuration with the window emptied (K of about 4 per zero below, i.e. the verified-height horizon), and it is blind to the prime data. Half-plane Pick kernels for Re z > a0 are implied by the support constraint. Weakest point: the domination constant is certified on a grid and on five node families plus 48 hill climbs, with only a factor 2.5 margin at (T,K) = (100,24).

title: Euler cone intersected with the functional equation in a window
note: Exact uniqueness is Hamburger's theorem and uses neither the cone nor multiplicativity. In one window [T,T+H], lattice translates zeta(s + 2 pi i k/log(T/2pi)) are cone elements with functional-equation defect about (|alpha|H + alpha^2)/(2T), so the feasible set at fixed tolerance grows with T; a window gives about 30 real conditions against about sqrt(T)/log T free primes, and a prescribed zero at 3/4 + i t0 is feasible (float64 model, T up to 1e6). lesson: The functional equation is linear in a(n) and the Euler cone is convex in log F, so "cone intersect affine space" holds in no single variable. A window of length H gives about 30 to 35 real conditions independent of T, against about sqrt(T)/log T free primes; pinning in one window needs H of Riemann-Siegel size. Windowed functional-equation tests cannot separate zeta from its lattice translates or from L(s, chi_5) at height T/5 (measured residual about 50/T). Stability around zeta can never exclude zeros uniformly because inf |zeta(3/4+it)| = 0. Multiplicativity only reduces N unknowns to pi(N) (cone pinned, relaxed model unpinned at T = 1e5 in the multi-height model).

lesson: Stage stability classes are invariant under torus rotations, and a unimodular twist is a rotation, so no stability tool reads the angles t log p. U lacks no per-prime property; it lacks joint linearity of the angles in log p at bounded slope. Height-uniformity (R2) forces any bound on G_P up to the trivial one, so R2 and bounded renormalised stages (R4) conflict at stage level; a usable statement must hold t fixed while P grows.

title: One-sided bound in P at a fixed strip point for the renormalised Euler stage
note: The Laplace transform in log P of G(P;s) has singular points w = 0 and w = rho - s for every zero at every height, so a one-sided bound Re G <= C P^alpha or >= -C P^alpha at one fixed point is equivalent (up to eps, with the exceptional ordinate t = gamma for the upper sign) to Theta <= sigma + alpha: the Landau target of rows T2/P10 in twisted form. lesson: The de Branges kernel about Re s = 1/2 needs the stage at the reflected point 1 - s, where the Euler product diverges; the functional equation is not an input of any finite stage. Each Euler factor is lossless about Re s = 0 only, and moving the axis to 1/2 turns the Paley-Wiener chain into negative squares one for one (density theta(X)/pi). Zeta's own Theta about 1/2 is a Moebius factor, so its space is rank one with or without RH: the negative-square count goes to infinity along the stages and to zero in the limit, which no monotone or semicontinuous device can follow. Unimodular twists, Liouville, E_a, RZ_b and Beurling fail at the same step as zeta, so the construction does not separate controls.

Differentiating the Hankel data in t does not change row Q4: the prime side is causal for every twist (argued) and the difference is the residue sum over zeros.
lesson: Reject combinations whose engine is a heat-monotone functional of the anticausal Hankel block or of zero configurations.

note: The m-reflection is target-blind Gauss-sum algebra (same for every eta and for DH). It lowers x only from points with 2x+z < 3/2 where nothing is known; every chamber it adds lies in x >= 3/2, so the hull abscissa equals the input. Its chamber is reached only by meromorphic continuation across the zeros of the Kubota normalising L-factor, and a hull of a meromorphy tube gives no control of the polar set. Existence of the functional equation for the full m-series is open; order-6 equations cannot be tested by dual lengths at norm 1e7 without the S-data matrix.
